title: Florida House, District 116
what_it_does: Represents District 116 (Part of Miami-Dade) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Ashley Perez-Biliskov
candidates.background: Ashley Perez-Biliskov is a first-generation Cuban American raised in Miami who worked for more than a decade as a medical speech-language pathologist. She holds degrees from Florida State University and the University of South Florida and is running to succeed her brother, House Speaker Daniel Perez, who is term-limited. She is not an incumbent; the seat's current holder is Daniel Perez.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

other_issues.title: Campaign themes
other_issues.summary: Her campaign materials emphasize accountable government and district concerns such as school funding, health care, public safety, property taxes and infrastructure, but she has not published detailed positions and did not answer the Vote411 questionnaire.

sources.title: Community Newspapers: Ashley Perez-Biliskov: A new voice for District 116

other_issues.title: Campaign message
other_issues.summary: Perez-Biliskov has campaigned on what she calls America First solutions to the challenges Florida families face, emphasizing her experience as a health-care professional, her perspective as a mother and what she describes as accountable government. Her campaign website and local profile coverage do not set out positions on specific bills or issues.

sources.title: Ashley Perez-Biliskov: A New Voice for District 116
Ashley Perez-Biliskov for State Representative District 116

candidates.name: Nicolas Ramos
candidates.background: Nicolas Ramos, 35, is the Democratic nominee for House District 116; he also ran for the seat in 2024, losing to House Speaker Daniel Perez. He filed in late May 2026 and answered the Vote411 questionnaire.
